subject: Learning Methods
title: Previewing Before Deep Study
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Previewing Before Deep Study.

hook.text: She skimmed the chapter headings for two minutes before reading. Her comprehension jumped 40 percent.

buildup.text: Previewing creates a mental scaffold. Your brain builds a framework that organizes incoming details.

discovery.text: Read headings, bold terms, and summaries first. Then dive in. Your brain fills a structure instead of building.

twist.text: Previewing feels like a waste of time. But it reduces total study time by making deep reading more efficient.

climax.text: Spend five minutes scanning structure before each chapter. Note what seems new and what looks familiar.

punchline.text: Skim the map first. Then explore the territory.

quiz.question: Why does previewing improve comprehension?
options: It warms up the visual cortex for reading
It builds a mental scaffold that organizes incoming details
It identifies the easiest sections to read first
